direction: Mechanism of verbalized confidence in decoder-only LLMs: is post-hoc-verbalized confidence a genuine self-evaluation cached at answer emission and later read out, or a cosmetic restatement computed on-demand from token log-probabilities?

behaviors.statement: When a decoder-only LLM is asked to verbalize its confidence in a numeric 0–100 form immediately after answering a factual question, the verbalized value is written into hidden states at post-answer positions (E0..E4) and later retrieved from that cache when the model speaks the confidence token (rather than being freshly computed at the confidence position from token log-probabilities or a fresh reading of the answer).
behaviors.behavior_conclusion: The behavior is real and taken as given: verbal confidence is a reproducible, non-trivial, non-constant black-box uncertainty signal in Gemma-3-27B-pt on TriviaQA (parse rate 0.997 across 3 seeds × 1500 items, std ≈ 40 on the 0–100 scale, answer accuracy ≈ 0.18). Beyond the elicitation, its INTERNAL mechanism dissociates: verbal confidence is STRONGLY linearly decodable from post-answer residual states (ridge probe R²=0.541 at E4L10 vs. log-prob-only baseline R²≈0), but the strong causal cache-and-retrieve claim does NOT hold on the tested interventions — patching, attention-blocking, single-site direction steering (argmax and logit-level), top-5-site steering, and joint 5-site simultaneous steering all fail to move verbal confidence appreciably (max joint |span| = 0.32 first-digit units < 0.5 threshold). The correct scientific reading is a DECODABILITY-vs-CAUSAL-CONTROL DISSOCIATION: verbal confidence is decodable but not strongly controllable under the tested single-site or joint low-rank interventions.

mechanisms.family: Probing / Residual Stream States + Causal Attribution / Patching + Causal Attribution / Ablation + Representation and Parameter Analysis / Steering Vectors
mechanisms.headline: Decodability–causal-control dissociation in Gemma-3-27B-pt: verbal-confidence value is linearly decodable at post-answer positions (probe R²=0.541 at E4L10, ΔR²=+0.542 over log-prob-only, Spearman ρ=0.696), but the same location is NOT causally privileged — residual patching yields signed effect 0.55 vs. 3.07 at a MID-question control (main/control ratio 0.24, plan required ≥3), attention-blocking cache→conf-gen collapses conf by only +0.19 (no prior-collapse), single-site steering α-span < 0.15 first-digit units across the top-5 sites individually (E4L10, E1L5, E2L5, E3L10, E3L5) and stays flat vs n=8 random-direction controls while capability preservation NLL delta < 0.02 nats/token, and joint 5-site simultaneous steering surfaces only a small distributed effect (max |span| 0.32 across seeds 42/123/2024, still below the 0.5 threshold) that single-site sweeps missed. The paper framing is 'decodable but not strongly controllable under tested interventions', not 'not causally used'.

claims.statement: For a decoder-only LLM asked to answer a question and then verbalize a confidence value, the residual-stream hidden states at post-answer positions already carry a linearly-decodable representation that determines the eventual verbalized confidence, and this representation is causally used by the confidence-generation step (rather than the confidence being freshly computed at the confidence token from token log-probabilities).
claims.method: Location screen — ridge probe over the 5 post-answer positions × 12 layers ([5,10,...,60]) predicting verbalized confidence, judged pass when peak cell R² clearly exceeds the log-prob-only baseline; Causal Intervention chain — residual-stream patching at the top-K cache sites with clean-high/corrupt-low pairs matched on n_answer_tokens, attention-block from cache→confidence-generation position, direction-steering with diff-of-means and LDA on α ∈ [-16,+16] (v2 hardened by capability probe on unrelated-continuation NLL and n=8 random-direction controls, v3 logit-level E[first_digit] closes sub-argmax loophole, joint 5-site steering via MultiSiteSteeringHook tests distributed control), each judged against pre-committed effect-size thresholds and MID-question matched controls.
claims.conclusion: Decodability holds strongly (probe R²=0.541 at post-answer position E4L10 with Spearman ρ=0.696, ΔR²=+0.542 over log-prob-only baseline ≈0), but single-site and joint causal control does not: residual patching main/control ratio=0.24 vs. required ≥3, attention-block cache→conf-gen mean shift only +0.19 with no prior-collapse, argmax steering flat vs. random-direction controls at capability delta < 0.02 nats/token, logit-level (sub-argmax) span < 0.01 at E4L10, top-5 single-site max |span| < 0.15, joint 5-site max |span| = 0.32 first-digit units below the 0.5 threshold — 'decodable but not strongly controllable' dissociation, with a small distributed joint effect leaving room for weak distributed causal sensitivity. Log-prob-restatement null downgraded to HOLD (M6c cross-seed values [3.57, 0.10, 0.43] fail variance gate).

untried_mechanism_directions: Tuning & Editing (rejected in round 1 as claim was diagnostic, not applied — but a calibration-improvement application would reopen this)
Formation Tracing (rejected in round 1 as claim was inference-time, not training-time — but tracing when the decodability emerges during pretraining could sharpen the dissociation)
Unit Interpretation (rejected in round 1 as label was already human-interpretable — but SAE / auto-interp on the decodable direction could recover WHICH features encode confidence)
Decision Auditing (rejected in round 1 as confidence WAS the output — but auditing whether verbalized confidence agrees with downstream user decisions would test its calibration in a different sense)
